content:
I have a use case for association lists embedded in dependent types so I need good decidability and extensionality properties. The complicated structure of the Std.Hash* family of types is not ideal because of the fact that it's difficult to reason about their extensionality and it's not always obvious how to prove the decidability of their properties and yet there is always an obvious proof on the list model; meanwhile the Ext version of these are hard to iterate on.

There are a number of non-Internalassociation list implementations: Batteries.AssocList, Lean.AssocList, AList, but it seems to me these lack the extensive theory of the Std.Data.Internal.List.Associative namespace, so I've been freely grabbing theorems from the Std.Data.Internal.List and Std.Data.DHashMap.Internal.AssocList namespaces instead. However since they belong to the Internal namespaces I've been thinking that maybe this isn't ideal although they perfectly correspond to my use case.

Does the fact that they are internal suggest that we shouldn't expect any guarantee of relative stability? Are there plans to eventually promote these to a user-facing API?

I believe we don't have plans to actively change them, but we don't guarantee for that as we haven't put the same amount of thought into naming, consistency and lemma coverage as we put into public APIs. Having these as public API is a reasonable wish that I remember having heard from other people, too. But I'm afraid that our backlog in the standard library team is long enough that we probably won't get to creating a public API in the next months.
That works, thanks a lot for answering!
